reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports lattice distortion and W-rich intermetallic formation in AlCoCrFeNiWx coatings at 800 °C, but the hypothesis concerns a CoCrFeNi matrix (no Al), a bulk alloy rather than a laser-clad coating, and a much lower W content (~0.5 at.% vs. x=0.5 in a different system). The oxide glaze mechanism and low-temperature benefits are not addressed by the cited passages, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Tungsten addition induces severe lattice distortion in CoCrFeNi-based HEAs
Tungsten addition promotes formation of fine W-rich intermetallic phases
Lattice distortion and intermetallics stabilize microstructure and improve wear resistance at high temperature
Modified microstructure drives formation of a protective oxide glaze at elevated temperatures
These effects will reduce friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C
